reviews.text: Thumbs up is basically because there's no "neutral" or "wait and see" option, and I don't want to help tank the score when a game with so much potential is in early access. Having said all that, I don't think it's in a state you should jump on right now unless it's just to support the devs (and I say that as an obsessive early access enjoyer who has been hanging out for S3K since it was announced). I'm not refunding, but I will put it down until we're a few updates in. To summarise, my meagre time with S3K went like this: [list] [*] blasted through 1st level, seems a bit slow but fun [*] got to second level, and am mobbed by dozens of Wolverine wannabes (for reference, Wolverine dudes do 10x the damage per tick that the basic ♥♥♥♥♥ enemies do) [*] The 2 weapons I have fire at the rate of roughly once per calendar year, and aren't even strong enough to kill most enemies in one hit [*] immediately die [/list] The fun in a Vampire Survivors clone is failing consistently until you get strong and/or aware enough to fail slightly [i]less[/i] consistently. [b]But[/b]. You should have fun while failing. Going splat over and over doesn't feel quite so yuck when you're mowing down hordes of enemies while digital fireworks tickle your eyeballs. It's how VS mashes the brain's "DOPAMINE" button over and over, even though the core gameplay is exceptionally simple. It [i]looks[/i] like you should get bored in 10 seconds flat, but gets some serious hooks into you, because there's a sense of experimentation and learning. Unfortunately, S3K has very tight restrictions on what abilities are available for purchase, and that's [i]before[/i] you introduce RNG for what shows up in shops. The mechanics I've discovered so far: [list] [*][b]Gameplay[/b] [list] [*] Chose a Jiggly boi and a Deck of ability cards. There are several slots for custom decks, but you start with only enough cards to make one deck. [*] Disregard enemies, acquire powerups. [*] Sufficiently disregard enemies until Uber-enemies appears. [*] Disregard Uber-enemy [*] Proceed to next level [*] Loop [/list] [*][b]Decks and Abilities[/b] [list] [*] Dictate what abilities appear in vending machines during the levels. [*] Consists of ranks D, C, B, A, and S ranks. Abilities correspond to these ranks, and each rank in you deck has 4 slots (so you pick 4 "D" rank cards, 4 "C" rank cards, ... , 4 "S" rank cards etc). Each slot must be filled. [*] You get coins by killing things. You spend coins to buy abilities from those in your deck. [*] This is done via vending machines which pop up at random during a level. [*] You can also spend coins to upgrade the vending machine (and future vending machines) which will add more choices to each vending machine, and increase the rank of available cards. [*] Getting three-of-a-kind abilities will cause them to merge, creating a single but more powerful ability. [/list] [*][b]Jiggly Bois[/b] [list] [*] Presumably they have strengths and weakness? [*] IDK, because there is only one available at the start, and I lost interest after the 5th time I died within 2 minutes on the second level. [*] during levels you collect DNA which apparently is meta-currency used to upgrade your Jiggly bois, but I couldn't see where to spend it? [/list] [/list] [*][b]How it plays out[/b] [list] [*] Basically, vampire survivors but suuuuuuuuuuper slow and frustrating. [*] All the basic weapons you begin with are sloooooooow. [*] All the basic weapons are weeeeeeaakkkk. [*] The starter Jiggly boi moves at about the same speed as continental drift. [*] Enemies either do no damage, or have tactical nukes strapped to each fist. [*] There are no real options or combinations to try from the start. [*] Maybe I'm missing something but for me, the second level sequence of events is: [list] [*] [00:00:00] Start level [*] [00:18:00] Gather enough coins to hit up a vending machine [*] [00:21:00] Buy a couple of weak-ass weapons to compliment my starting weak-ass weapon. [*] [00:23:00] Turn around, and have my every unplugged orifice filled by Wolverine claws. (not sure how many orifices a nebulous mass of goo has, but the key take-away is that death is exceedingly swift). [/list] [/list] [b]Summary[/b] There's definitely some brilliance hiding here; I really like the idea of the decks as opposed to giving the player the ability to banish skills per VS et al. The pixel art is gorgeous, and the sound design is great (the death noises of humans are hilarious tbh). Music is brilliant. Aesthetically, everything ties together really, really well. I personally feel the mechanics just need a lot more work: [list] [*] Everything is too slow. Movement speed, projectile speed, cooldown speed. It's supposed to be a horde shooter, but I have time to go make a cup of tea between shots from the starting weapons. This wouldn't be a problem, except: [*] The hordes ramp super fast, and there is a huuuuuuuuuge variance between the damage enemies do. [*] Nothing in the starting kit feels fun to use. At all. It's the absolute opposite of an early-game hook. [*] The starting kit needs a few more options to allow players to start experimenting early on. [/list] Right now, It's a (visually and aurally gorgeous) horde shooter (with a lot of potential) that won't let you shoot hordes. :(

I want to like this game, but the card unlocks take FOREVER. I need to go from 400k -> 600k exp to get my next card unlock and I'm only getting around 40k per victory. Not to mention I cannot unlock any more characters due to lacking the required cards to meet the "4 different X abilities at level 3" which requires me to grind exp and hope that it's one of my next unlocks. Upgrades in the skill menu are also unlocked by needing X amount of a specific card type, which once again is locked behind the exp grind.
I really need to stop buying games by Konfa. Their understanding of how much grinding is fun is clearly way off from mine, because their games just all seem to be way too slow-paced for me.

[H1]《史莱姆3000》：真正的“粑粑”幸存者[/H1] 《Slime 3K: Rise Against Despot》是由Konfa Games开发、tinyBuild发行的一款糅杂了卡牌管理的幸存者游戏，游戏的美术风格独树一帜，但在难度曲线上有些让玩家郁闷。 [H2]像素外星人再出发：名为「暴君」的艺术[/H2] 翻开Konfa Games以往的作品序列，你就会发现[B]这家工作室那充满着个人特色的美术风格：扭曲的外星生物、赛博霓虹味的配色、还有到处飞溅的荧绿色血浆[/B]。从本作的名字《Slime 3K: Rise Against Despot》中，我们也可以看到对工作室前两作《Despotism 3k》和《Despot's Game》的一脉相承，不过除了第一部《暴君3K》以外，《暴君的游戏》跟本次的《史莱姆3k》都主抓游戏性而没有在剧情上下功夫，未能继续拓展暴君世界观稍显遗憾。 [H2]局内的构筑选项由你决定！[/H2] 本作还有一个比较有意思的设定，就是提出了一个「卡组」概念，玩家可以在赛前选择当局游戏内会出现的技能卡，让构筑朝着自己期望的方向进行。[B]游戏的技能卡有品质（D-S）和等级（1-3）两个属性，[/B]其中等级是类似于自走棋的合成机制，三个1级合成2级，当合成到3级以后这张卡片将不再刷新；品质则代表技能卡在商店内的刷新顺序，要不断提升商店等级才能刷新高品质技能卡。 因此本作的破关思路基本比较统一：先把廉价技能抓满升到3级，然后升级商店、尽快刷出高级技能，实现预期中的强力构筑。不过构筑过程也是与游戏进行程度基本挂钩，所以玩家每次的游玩体验都大差不厘。 [H2]碾碎敌人，或者被敌人淹死[/H2] 跟一般的幸存者相比，[B]《Slime 3K》有一个很大的优势就是玩家可以在早起就实现无双——不过与前期无双相对应的则是后期的暴毙，难度曲线上有点不走寻常路的味道。[/B]在游戏过程中，玩家基本上不用担心被碰到怪物掉血，因为你常常会在怪海里洗澡，通过拾取加速、商店、炸弹、加血等道具来获得各种增益。 但是后期则会莫名其妙地被怪海堆死。你明明感觉自己构筑也还不错，但看着这些铺满整个屏幕（是的，真正意义上的整个屏幕）的扭曲小人们把自己的史莱姆淹没，你会感到宛如贤者时光般的虚脱——暴毙总是来的如此突然，尤其它还没让你爽到就已经嘎屁了。明明之前还是血量一点不带掉的无双战神，突然之间怪海就感觉上升了一个层级，绵软的小手枪雄风不再，只能满地图找血包然后饮恨暴毙。 [H2]我的技能在打些什么？[/H2] 《Slime 3K》作为一款幸存者游戏而言，个人认为还有个比较突出的问题：[B]击中反馈不足[/B]。玩家的技能即使是升到满级看起来也跟一个小水管无异，远远达不到寻常幸存者的清屏效果，[B]由于构筑过低的存在感再加上像素风格导致的低辨识度，甚至可能你都认不清技能卡对应的攻击技能长些什么样[/B]。相比之下，你在游戏中拾取到的各种增益道具或许才是你的最佳伙伴，尤其是细胞炸弹有如原子弹般在怪海中蹦出的高额伤害会让你更加感慨自己那小水管的乏力输出。 [H2]不合理的难度与背后的必然[/H2] 总的来说，[B]《Slime 3K》的糟糕体验主要来自于难度曲线的不合理[/B]。一方面是关卡之间，比如评论区很多提到的第四关难度陡增的问题；但更多我觉得还是游戏单局内的恶劣曲线：幸存者理论上应该是一个倒U曲线，前期简单、中期困难、成型以后割草；但在本作中游戏的难度是断崖式的，比如游戏中影响最大的掉落道具，前面是感觉道具溢出捡不过来，等被怪海淹没以后却满地图都找不到最后的救命稻草。 其实[B]从Konfa Games以往的作品类型上，就充满着追赶热点的讨巧：[/B]肉鸽、模拟经营、自走棋，似乎所有的财富密码都尝试过，但显然这不是一家年轻工作室所能驾驭的。而这次他们做幸存者还不够，必须要加入点卡牌意思意思，因此在游戏性上失败也是在所难免。既然都没有搞明白类型的精髓在哪，不如先深耕某个领域，打磨好了再去下个赛道。 [H2]总结[/H2] 《Slime 3K》的美术的确亮眼，音乐也十分劲爆，从制作规格上算是一款素质还不错的独立游戏。但是Konfa Games的确不懂幸存者，玩家在游玩过程中既体会不到构筑的快感、也不能享受后期成型以后的割草快乐，游戏诡异的难度曲线让多数时刻下玩家会感到功亏一篑的挫败。而如果一款幸存者让玩家感到「不爽」，某种程度上已经算是违背了《吸血鬼幸存者》的祖训。 [quote] 执笔勾墨色，挥毫著文章；阳春布德泽，璞玉生光辉 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44174077/]吟遊诗人的手札[/url]，书游戏特色，写游戏魅力 [/quote]

1、最大的缺点：绝大部分技能和被动都和“主角是个史莱姆”这个设定无关，对于现在的技能池来说，把主角换成任意一种生物都一样，“主角是个史莱姆”作为游戏唯一的特色，还没有发挥出来 2、第6关和第10关数值膨胀严重，纯粹的数值没调好 3、相对17.2元的价格来说中规中矩的游戏，不算好玩但能玩，隐藏被动的玩法带来了一些Build的价值，我实在没法想象没有更新隐藏被动玩法之前，这游戏发售的前一个半月到底有多无聊 4、刷经验解锁更多技能的玩法不是不行，但这经验数值的设定，肝的也太见鬼了，所有技能解锁所需经验抹掉一个0还差不多

只能说很有潜力； 希望能标注解锁后隐藏能力的激活条件，方便构筑； 比起吸血鬼幸存者，目前不同技能之间的互动，没有感觉出来； 期待更新， 目前不是很推荐。

这不算是个成功的幸存者类游戏。 游戏提出了一个有趣的“卡组”概念，玩家可以在赛前选择技能卡，构筑自己的游戏策略。然而，游戏的构筑过程与游戏进程挂钩，导致玩家每次的体验都相似。 前期玩家可以轻松实现无双，但后期难度陡增，常常会被怪物淹没。此外，击中反馈不足，技能看起来效果微弱，导致玩家对技能卡的攻击效果感到困惑。 技能卡的升级方式也是十分的蛋疼，需要规划剩余空位数量，运气不好时常会便秘。 总的来说，游戏的不合理难度曲线是其主要问题。关卡之间难度差异大，游戏内难度曲线也呈现断崖式变化。 尽管游戏的美术和音乐表现出色，但从玩家体验来看，游戏未能提供构建和后期的满足感。游戏难度曲线的诡异让玩家感到挫败。对于一款幸存者游戏来说，让玩家感到“不爽”已经违背了其基本原则。

I really want to like this game. I love the match 3 system for powerups and the visual style is awesome, but I just can't. I see the devs read reviews sometimes so want to be as constructive as possible. The whole point, I think, of these games is to feel the power of smashing through huge waves of baddies with a variety of ridiculous weapons and powers and after a few hours with this I still haven't felt that. A couple of times it came close but all I was rewarded with was an unplayable framerate and then the boss dies and that's it start again on new level. The UI, oh my the UI, is not good the skill selection menu compressed into a small box in the centre screen which makes it seem cluttered. There's no colour coding on the various skill attributes which makes it difficult to see what goes with what without hovering over everything I'd rather the attributes were colour coded than the level of them. Greying out everything when you have no points to purchase is another issue again requires hovering to read. Having to click then confirm either buy or lock is frustrating and slows down the game, I'd rather just rightclick lock left click buy. I also loathe having to hold R to switch to autoaim and that I have to do it every single time I start, this could be an option in the menu ala Halls of Torment and can be switched in game. It's also difficult to know what skills will actually combine into something as I cannot see them listed anywhere so it's a guessing game but a frustrating one. You also can only hover over for the tooltip when in the buying menu no pressing escape to check things out. When you make a match it automatically puts it in the inactive list of skills for utterly no reason which I often miss and end up with my best ability in the inactive list. Picking up a chest from bosses which gives abilities is infuriating as 9/10 I have a full board and have no option to sell them for points or anything just makes me not want to pick things up which is hard to avoid as you need to dodge enemies or if your build demands you be close to them and auto collect when they die. The Grind. This game seems very grindy I feel like I need all the upgrades to actually get the powerfantasy but they come so slowly unlike Vampire Survivors where I feel I only need those boosts much later in the game. Also not being able to deselect them individually is irritating. This is all compounded by there being no stat boosts you can pick up in level. The deck building aspect does nothing for me and I vastly prefer the system in VS but it's mostly because I can't just build decks I want I have to keep playing to unlock skills, also not being able to manually rename decks but only pick from a preset list of names... why? Seriously why can't I call decks what I want? I've put 4 hours in and honestly I feel like I've seen enough. I've no idea if there is a survival mode or somesuch that might be more enjoyable, might be an unlock for finishing the game but I just don't really feel compelled to keep going. There also seems to only be the one map so you'll be looking at the same backdrop the entire time. Honestly I feel mostly frustrated playing this more than anything and with other games in the genre by the hour in mark I'm feeling like a boss but in this I just feel like I don't get it despite understanding the mechanics. I bought this with Despots Game in a pack and much like that game I can see there's a kernal of something great in there but it's just not being brought out though I will say at least this game is priced appropriately which Despots game certainly isn't. I'm optimistic more updates or a sequel might change the game a bit but for now I'd say this is a crowded market and Slime3K doesn't seperate itself from the pack. As I said at the start I want to love this game it has a lot going for it but something didn't come together in the execution. If you're looking for a game like this I'd say Vampire Survivors, Twenty Mins til Dawn, Hall of Torment, and Brotato are all much better bets and just less frustrating over all.

I've played only one game that I remember, on this style: Vampire Survivors, and that one does pretty much everything much, much better. This one, for a positive side, has better graphics, I really like the pixel graphics, character design and colour palette, but the gameplay fails to be fun. These kind of games is ALL about the weapons, and this game in particular fails miserably in providing fun or even useful weapons. There are a lot of ineffective or redundant weapons. Some just change the look of the effect, but they're just more of the same. I couldn't find a combination effective enough to stop the hordes that are thrown at me, nothing seems to be effective. It looks like a very heavy grinding game, but I don't even see a goal to get something that will make me powerful enough. In terms of the stages, I didn't find anything in any of them, so thy're basically an arena with nothing to explore, do or find.. There no active weapons, or shields, or dodge movement, nothing.. Jut move around, barely being able to avoid damage, running from pick up to pick up and getting the same weapons over and over again.. I spent the 5 hours to get through 3 levels, playing them countless times, until I realised I wasn't really having fun at all. It's a shame, I thought this could be as fun as V.S., but not even close. Go get that one instead! Not refunding because I've only payed $1, but honestly, I'm not interested in playing this any more..

A fabulous, incredibly charming little bullet-heaven game, especially for the price. It has some deckbuilding and auto-battler elements and, like all Konfa Games, comes with a fantastic art style and a pretty steep learning curve. It took me a while to really understand how to min-max the systems at play, but once you do it's pretty satisfying. It's a fairly small game, only twenty levels, but some of them are pretty hefty roadblocks that require you to use different builds. My only complaint is that progression feels relatively slow: You will sometimes have to grind just to unlock new abilities to improve your decks, and I managed to beat all 20 levels without unlocking every weapon, which was a little sad. Great timekiller. Not groundbreaking by any means, but it's a very solid game for bullet-heaven fans that want a challenge. Can't wait to see what's next in the Despot's series.

I was stuck on level 10 for quite some time. This is not a bad place to be -- it's the best level for farming DNA, and very good for XP -- every failure unlocked a card -- but the experience wasn't great: I could do the level itself fine, and then the green flowers that spawned with the boss would surround and murder me, and I couldn't do enough damage to make a real dent in them. I got through by seeing a video of someone playing the game in a completely different way: it seems a limited number of enemies can spawn at a time, so if you wait for the chainsaw enemies to spawn en masse, then flee to the opposite side of the map and kite them in a circle, much fewer enemies will spawn in front of you. If you repeat until the boss spawns, you get a wave of green enemies with the boss, then birds spawning for a while, then a wave of flowerpeople, and then eventually they stop spawning and you can kill the remnants and the boss. I found the rest of the levels far easier, including the "yes, this is possible" level 13, which I trounced with lasers. As more cards unlocked I saw more things I could have done -- the "Trash Throwing" card gives the laser 8x damage, which does 1200 damage, and together with the "shot" and "targeted" bonuses tears through the damage sponges. Having 5 level 3 darkness cards unlocks an upgrade that gives darkness cards +100% damage, which again is enough to tear through them. Still, all of these needed cards I didn't have unlocked when I first encountered the level. There are some controls I didn't see noted anywhere -- in the shop you can tap space to restock, or hold to upgrade, enter buys, the A and D keys navigate through the cards, and escape exits. F locks / unlocks. I liked the achievement variety and how it encouraged different playstyles. It would have been nice if Black Swordsmen showed up somewhere else than failing to kill the boss on level 6, but making a deck that can only kill extremely close enemies and running away from the boss was also interesting, though I did have to play the level a few times. I would have appreciated options to reduce the opacity of the attacks / enemies, as you see on other games like this. At the end it can get rather busy and hard to spot bonuses in the crowd.

Blueballed by a survivor-like The first few hours of the game are pretty decent. You see the amount of cards, the passive bonus system for building cards with specific tags, a handful of characters, edgy humor. Then you play a few more hours and you are facing imbalanced levels that either force you to grind meta-upgrades and play with an exact build, or letting you pass absolutely blindly. Unlockable cards are in an okayish state. but a big amount of them feel purely cosmetic. The tag system is great, making your card building process more complicated, but the amount of actually useful tags is critically small. Pickable activities are a good addition that make you roam around the map and not just stay in one place. The game had a lot of potential, but it did not deliver well.
